title: Fake-hou residency - the defect was a re-import, not a stub
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). The release condition R42 names is met and was measured, not inferred: the AttributeError at component_builder.py:315 / scene_template.py:218 is gone under hython3.13, tests/solaris/test_live_wiring.py drives real `hou` (27/27), the gate suite holds at 4889 passed / 0 failed (up from 4881, Commandment 7 satisfied), and every regression pin fails against a deliberate break (18/18 mutation matrix, 4 controls green). Two things this receipt does NOT claim: the shipping suite is not green (98 failed, unchanged environment buckets - it was never a ratchet floor per R40), and 4 tests that were green in the pre-fix run are now red. Those 4 are decorations unmasked by removing the residency, not regressions; the evidence is below and the disposition is a ruling item.

the_headline.claim_before: R41/R42: `hou.Parm.set` exists on 22.0.368, yet component_builder.py:315 raises AttributeError - 'a STUB Parm is shadowing the real class', the same mechanism Q1 fixed for PySide6.
the_headline.what_it_actually_was: No stub was involved. `hou.py` executed a SECOND time in the process. That re-ran `_hou.Parm_swigregister(Parm)`, re-pointing the C extension's type registry at a NEW `Parm` class object; then `hou.py:123810 __finishImport()` RAISED (`type object 'PerfMonProfile' has no attribute 'save'` - the deprecation wrappers are not re-appliable), leaving that class HALF-BUILT at 166 attributes against the original's 186, with no `.set`. importlib discarded the failed module, the test restored the original object correctly BY OBJECT, and from that moment `sys.modules['hou']` and `hou.Parm` looked perfect - `hou.Parm.set` True - while `node.parm('x')` returned instances of the zombie class.
the_headline.why_the_positive_control_and_the_failure: R41's control probed the MODULE (`hou.Parm.set` -> True). The casualty was the C-level type registry, which no module-level introspection can see. That gap is the entire finding, and it is why the defect read as a shadowing stub.
the_headline.the_deeper_lesson: Q1's law was 'restore-by-object, not restore-by-reimport'. This leg extends it: for `hou`, restore-by-object is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. The damage lands at the moment of the re-import, in the C extension, past anything sys.modules can express. The re-import is what must not happen.

root_cause.producer: harness/notes/residency_trace.py (pytest plugin) + direct hython probes, both reproduced independently by the workflow's root-cause lens in a fresh hython with no conftest loaded
reproduction: hython3.13 -c "import sys, hou; n=hou.node('/obj').createNode('geo','g1'); saved=sys.modules.pop('hou'); import hou  # raises; sys.modules['hou']=saved; p=n.parm('ty')"
-> reimport RAISES: AttributeError type object 'PerfMonProfile' has no attribute 'save'
-> sys.modules hou is original: True ; real.Parm has set: True   <- the innocent-looking state
-> instance class is original Parm: False ; has set: False ; n_attrs 166 vs 186   <- the casualty

two_routes_in.a_eviction: `hou` absent from sys.modules, then `import hou`. Original module object survives untouched; the C type registry is the casualty. This is the route that caused the 17 failures.
two_routes_in.b_reload: `importlib.reload(hou)` with `hou` PRESENT. Reaches sys.meta_path anyway, and is STRICTLY NASTIER - reload re-executes into the SAME namespace, so `hou.Parm` ITSELF becomes the zombie. VERIFIED-RUNTIME: after a raised reload, `hou.Parm is <original>` -> False, dir() 166 vs 186, no `.set`. Nothing in the tree reloads `hou` today; it is pinned so the coverage is by design rather than by luck.

two_distinct_defects.note: Both are real; only one is causal for the 17. Stated separately so the commit narrative cannot be read as claiming the residency trace explained the AttributeError - it did not, and the workflow's root-cause and adjudicator lenses both flagged that risk.

findings.summary: `hou.py` must never execute twice in one process. A second execution re-registers the SWIG type map to a half-built `Parm` class (166 attrs vs 186, no `.set`) and every later `node.parm(...).set(...)` in the process raises AttributeError, while all module-level introspection stays healthy.
findings.status: FIXED - structurally prevented, not merely repaired at the call sites.

findings.anchor: tests/conftest.py (the guard's own comment, as first written)
findings.summary: My own documentation was wrong: the finder is NOT 'consulted ONLY when hou is absent'. `importlib.reload(hou)` reaches sys.meta_path with `hou` PRESENT, and corrupts the module IN PLACE (`hou.Parm` itself becomes the zombie) rather than leaving it pristine. Found by the root-cause lens, then verified independently by me before acting.
findings.status: FIXED - comment corrected, and test_reimport_guard_covers_importlib_reload pins the route so the coverage is by design rather than by accident. Mutation M10 proves the pin fails if the guard is narrowed.

findings.summary: The FAKE_HOU_RESIDENCY_GUARD returned early whenever this conftest had not planted - i.e. under hython, the one interpreter where a resident fake is a real defect rather than a tidiness question. A check that could not fail exactly where the failure lives, inside the guard written to enforce Law 1.
findings.status: FIXED - armed in both modes, compares by object identity.

Its own docstring reasoned that the residency guard 'never sees the gap' - correct, and precisely why the idiom was dangerous: the damage happens inside the gap, not at collection_finish. findings.anchor: tests/conftest.py:25 HOUDINI_BUILD default; tests/test_lop_flywheel.py, tests/test_m3_logs_doctor.py, tests/test_wiring_flywheel.py
findings.summary: FOUR TESTS WERE GREEN ONLY BECAUSE A FAKE `hou` WAS RESIDENT. They are now red. They are decorations in exactly F4's sense - they passed because a fake could not disagree - and removing the residency exposed them. NOT regressions from this fix.
findings.proof_not_regression: Run in isolation under hython they fail IDENTICALLY on the pre-fix tree and the post-fix tree - 4 failed, 1 passed, both trees, same command (producer: git stash push -- tests/ around the same hython pytest invocation). A change cannot be the cause of a failure that predates it.
findings.mechanism: conftest.py:25 `HOUDINI_BUILD = os.environ.get('SYNAPSE_TEST_HOUDINI_BUILD', '21.0.671')` defaults to H21. With a fake `hou` resident, version resolution fell back to H21 and matched the constant. With real `hou` resident it correctly resolves H22 and disagrees: `assert '22.0.368' == '21.0.671'`, `assert '21.0.671' in 'stamp 22.0.368 ...'`. Tier for the mechanism: VERIFIED-DERIVED; tier for the isolation control: VERIFIED-RUNTIME.
findings.refutation_recorded: The adjudicator proposed instead that the BEFORE run had SYNAPSE_TEST_HOUDINI_BUILD set and the AFTER run did not. REFUTED: the variable is unset in this environment and every run in this leg was launched from one shell with one environment (producer: `env | grep SYNAPSE` -> nothing but PWD/OLDPWD). The isolation control outranks the inference either way.
findings.status: OPEN - disposition is for_ruling RES-R1. Not fixed here: it is a different defect class (H21 constants pinned while running H22) and fixing it silently would be scope expansion.

findings.summary: Load-sensitive flake, not a regression. Failed in 1 of 3 full shipping samples, passed in the other 2, and passes 3/3 in isolation. Recorded so a future ratchet run that trips it is not misread as collateral damage from this leg. Matches the repo's known threads+sleeps pattern.
findings.status: OPEN - noted, not fixed. No action proposed in this leg.

findings.summary: The merge ratchet regex-parses 'N passed' / 'N failed' out of pytest's output and does not consult the return code. A run aborted by either guard exits 4 with the normal 'N passed' summary and zero 'failed' tokens, so the ratchet scores it as holding. Found by the pin-quality lens, confirmed by the adjudicator.
findings.mitigation_shipped: The static eviction ban (test_no_test_evicts_hou_from_sys_modules) is an ordinary test failure, which the ratchet DOES count, and it runs on the gate interpreter where the guards never arm. So the defect class this leg closes is enforceable in CI regardless of the rc hole.
findings.status: OPEN - for_ruling RES-R2. Not fixed here: it is a guardrail defect wider than this leg, and harness/verify/ is the ratchet's own territory.

findings.summary: The module-swap tracer found the FIRST form of the defect and was structurally incapable of finding the second. A pop -> import -> restore-by-object entirely inside one test body produces no transition at any pytest boundary, so rt_full_before.json contains zero rows for the two evictions that actually caused the 17 failures. Recorded so 'all transitions accounted for' is never read as a completeness claim. The `Parm_mutation` sampling added later is the right instrument and is retained.
findings.status: ACKNOWLEDGED - the instrument's limit is documented in the file.

findings.summary: The solaris live tests write USD layers into the REPO ROOT (shot_layers/), untracked and not gitignored, so every hython suite run dirties the working tree. Classified, not deleted (Law 4: census output is a hypothesis and deletion is a separate, human-confirmed act).

for_ruling.question: The 4 tests unmasked by RES-F7 pin H21 constants while running on H22. Fix in this leg, fix in H2, or re-scope conftest.py:25's HOUDINI_BUILD default?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - a value judgement between defensible options, not something provable from the tree. It is a different defect class from fake-hou residency, and R42 narrowed this leg's release condition to the residency clause precisely so unrelated untidiness would not gate it. Fixing it here would be the scope expansion R42 was written to prevent; leaving it silent would be worse.
for_ruling.recommendation: Deposit to H2. H2 is the F1-F11 re-qualification and these are exactly the class of claim it exists to re-qualify - tests that agreed with a mock. The cheapest correct fix is probably to resolve HOUDINI_BUILD from the live `hou` when one is resident rather than defaulting to a literal, but that changes what a large number of tests assert and belongs in a leg that can measure it.

for_ruling.question: check_suite_baseline ignores pytest's return code (RES-F9). Fix the ratchet, or accept that guard aborts are invisible to it?
for_ruling.why_escalated: harness/verify/ is the ratchet's own territory and a change there alters the merge gate's behaviour for every future leg - a value judgement about the guardrail, not a fact about this defect.
for_ruling.recommendation: Fix it: treat a non-zero pytest rc as not-green in check_suite_baseline. It is a Law 1 hole in the instrument that enforces Law 6. This leg is insulated from it by the static eviction ban, but the next guard to be added will not be.

for_ruling.question: shot_layers/ is written into the repo root by the solaris live tests (RES-F11). Gitignore it, redirect the tests to tmp_path, or leave it?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Trivial to fix three different ways; which one is right depends on whether those layers are ever inspected after a run. Not my call, and Law 4 forbids me deleting the files to find out.
for_ruling.recommendation: Redirect to tmp_path - a test that writes into the repo root will eventually be committed by accident. Gitignoring hides it rather than fixing it.
